segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: hey [NAME] how're you doing

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: i'm doing alright aside from this elbow pain

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: so it looks like here that you came in to see us today for an evaluation of that right elbow pain can you tell me can you can you tell me well first of all what do you think has been causing that pain

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: so i really during this pandemic i really got into ceramics and doing pottery so i've been doing a lot of pottery and over the past week i then started to develop this elbow pain

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: okay and then so tell me a little bit more about that elbow pain where does it hurt exactly

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: you know it hurts a lot in the inside of my elbow

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: okay so the inside of your right elbow okay

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: yeah

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: and then does the pain radiate down your arm or up into your shoulder or anything like that

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: it does n't go into my shoulder it's it stays mostly at my elbow but it can go down a bit into my forearm

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: okay and then do you remember any trauma did you hit your arm or elbow or any on anything

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: no nothing i i really was trying to think if there is anything else and i ca n't think of anything

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: okay and you've never injured that right elbow before

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: no

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: alright so now let's talk a little bit about your pain and how bad it how bad is that pain on a scale from zero to ten ten being the worst pain you've ever felt in your life

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: i would say probably a six

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: okay and does that pain keep you up at night

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: it does

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: okay and when you have that kind of pain does it keep you from doing other type of activities

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: yeah i mean i still try to like work through with using my arm but yeah it's it's it's difficult for me sometimes to lift and do things because of that pain

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: okay and then and how long has this pain been going on

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: about four days now

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: alright and anything you've done to help relieve or alleviate that pain any anything that that's giving you relief

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: i've tried ibuprofen that helps a little but not much

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: okay so if it's okay with you i would like to do a a quick physical exam your vitals look good and i'm gon na do a focused exam on that right elbow i'm gon na go ahead and and and press here do you do you have any pain when i press here

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: yes i do

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: okay so you are positive for pain to palpation you do note that moderate tenderness of the medial epicondyle now i'm gon na have you turn your wrist as if you're turning a door knob do you have any pain when you do that

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: not really

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: okay now turn your wrist in so do you have any pain when you do that

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: yeah that hurts

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: okay so you do have pain you were positive for pain when you pronate that that that forearm okay i'm gon na go ahead and have you rest your arm on the table here palm side up now i want you to raise your hand by bending at the wrist and i'm gon na put some resistance against it do you have any pain when i press against your flexed wrist

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: yes i do

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: alright so you are positive for pain with resistance against flexion of that left wrist so i let let's go ahead and review the x-ray that we did of your elbow the good news is i do n't see any fracture or bony abnormality of that right elbow which is good so let's talk a little bit about my assessment and plan for you so for the problem with elbow pain i do believe that this is consistent with medial epicondylitis which is caused by the overuse and potential damage of those tendons that bend

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: that that bend the wrist towards the palm now i want you to rest it i'm gon na order a sling and i want you to wear the sling while you're awake now we're also gon na have you apply ice to the elbow for twenty minutes three times a day and i want you to take ibuprofen that's gon na be six hundred milligrams q.6 h.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: with food and i want you to take that for a full week now you're not gon na like this part but i want you to hold off for the next couple of weeks on doing any type of pottery work okay alright now what i wan na do is i wan na see you again in a week and i wan na see how you're doing okay

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: alrighty

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: alrighty so i'll have the nurse come in and get you set up with that sling and i will see you again in about a week

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: alright thank you

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: thank you

reference_redacted.subjective:
Right elbow pain.

[NAME] is a pleasant 45-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right elbow pain.

Over the past week, the patient has developed 6/10 pain in the "inside" of his right elbow. The pain may radiate into his forearm on occasion, but does not extend up to his shoulder. He denies any history of trauma or injury, but he did start making pottery during the COVID-19 pandemic and suspects that his symptoms could be related to that. His symptoms affect his ability to lift objects or perform his typical activities of daily living. Ibuprofen provides minimal symptomatic relief.

The patient reports that he began making pottery during the COVID-19 pandemic.

The patient reports that he has been taking ibuprofen.

Musculoskeletal: Reports right elbow pain.
reference_redacted.objective:
Normal

MSK: Examination of the right elbow: Moderate tenderness at the medial epicondyle. No pain with supination of the forearm. Pain with pronation of the forearm. Pain with resistance against flexion of the wrist.

X-ray imaging of the right elbow was obtained and reviewed in office today. These reveal no evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.
reference_redacted.plan:
The patient and I discussed his diagnosis in detail, and I explained that his symptoms are likely caused by overuse and potential damage of the tendons. We will provide him with sling to be worn during the day while he is awake. I want him to take ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours with food for a full week and ice the elbow for 20 minutes, 3 times daily. Finally, I advised the patient to rest his elbow and avoid doing any pottery for the next couple of weeks.

The patient will follow up in 1 week.
